query: Which behavioral parameter ranges for labor supply, retirement and migration responses should we use, and how should we present sensitivity and partial-identification bounds where identification is weak?

response.query: Which behavioral parameter ranges for labor supply, retirement and migration responses should we use, and how should we present sensitivity and partial-identification bounds where identification is weak?
response.answer: For labor supply, retirement, and migration responses, use ranges based on empirical studies; present sensitivity and partial-identification bounds with confidence intervals. Use standard economic models for weak identification.

Message to the Quality Payment Program listserv on January 4, 2025, entitled “The Centers for Medicare & Medicaid Services (CMS) is Soliciting Stakeholder Recommendations for Potential Consideration of New Specialty Measure Sets and/or Revisions to the Existing Specialty Measure Sets for the 2026 Performance Year of the Merit-based Incentive Payment System (MIPS).”. Section 101(b) of the Medicare Access and CHIP Reauthorization Act of 2015 (MACRA) sunset the Medicare EHR Incentive Program for Eligible Professionals, set forth at section 1848(o) of the Act. As discussed previously, section 1848(o)(2) of the Act has been incorporated into the MIPS Promoting Interoperability performance category's requirements via section 1848(q)(2)(B)(iv) of the Act. See CY 2017 Quality Payment Program final rule (81 FR 77018 and 77019) for more information regarding the sunsetting of the Medicare EHR Incentive Program for Eligible Professionals.
